blocks.heading: Organisational conflict
blocks.text: Organisational conflict is disagreement by individuals or groups within the organisation. It can concern pay, conditions, resources, objectives, responsibilities or treatment. It is not the organisation chart or the mere existence of different departments. Conflict need not become industrial action: discussion can reveal misunderstandings and resolve differences. Some disagreement can identify real problems, but unmanaged conflict can damage cooperation, attendance and customer service. Identify the parties and the issue before proposing a remedy.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Iha Goods’ sales team wants rapid dispatch while production staff object that the proposed deadline prevents quality checks. The disagreement over priorities is conflict. The reporting relationship between the teams is part of structure, a different concept.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain the distinction: Tula Goods’ chart places supervisors below a manager, while staff disagree with management over shift allocations.

The chart describes organisational structure, the allocation of roles and reporting. The shift disagreement is organisational conflict. A reporting hierarchy can exist without that dispute, and naming hierarchy does not define the disagreement.
